newsitem.title: INDONESIA: NO REVIEW OF INDONESIA LABOUR LEADER'S CASE-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: NO REVIEW OF INDONESIA LABOUR LEADER'S CASE-REPORT.

text.p: Indonesia's Supreme Court has said it will not review the conviction of independent labour leader Mucthar Pakpahan on charges that he incited workers to strike, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Chief Justice Sarwata was quoted by the newspaper as saying the Supreme Court could only consider a review if a request is made by a government institution.
"If I permit a ruling on a request made by an individual, then I would have committed collusion," Sarwata said while answering reporters questions. He did not elaborate.

Lawyers for Pakpahan last week began proceedings in the East Jakarta State Court asking the court to process a request to the Supreme Court to review its decision in October 1996 to re-instate his four-year jail sentence for inciting riots in April 1994.
Pakpahan was jailed by a court in Medan, North Sumatra for three years in 1994 for inciting anti-Chinese riots.
The Medan High Court boosted the sentence to four years, but the Supreme Court then freed him in April 1995 and quashed his conviction in September that year.

However, in an unprecedented move, the Supreme Court reversed its earlier decision in October 1996 and upheld the conviction. The decision came after Pakpahan was arrested on subversion charges, which carry a maximum penalty of death. That arrest came after riots in Jakarta last year.

Pakpahan, whose subversion trial was suspended after he was hospitalised in March for various ailments, has told the the East Jakarta State Court he has new evidence to show he did not provoke the Medan riots in which one person died.
Indonesia has rejected offers from the United States and European trade unions for Pakpahan to be sent overseas for sophisticated medical tests and treatment.
